full_judgment:
3. The case of the defendant, in short, is that the plaintiff voluntarily got married with him after changing her religious status from Hindu to Muslim. The defendant bought eighteen kathas of land in the name of plaintiff by his own money, Tk. 3,20,000/- (three lac twenty thousand) only. At the time of marriage the defendant gave the ornament of Tk. 50,000/- (fifty thousand). The defendant also built the house by his own money on the land which was purchased in the name of plaintiff. The plaintiff is a nurse and she spent her money for maintenance of her mother and sister. Now the plaintiff has unholy connection with other persons and illegally tried to dissolve the marriage. The plaintiff has no right to file this suit for dissolution of marriage. The plaintiff according to Muslim Sharia law on 20.10.1983 got married with the defendant and now they are living in their house as husband and wife. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the order of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bagha, Rajshahi the plaintiff-opposite party filed a Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2007 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Rajshahi which was subsequently transferred to the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi. 

 7. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Rajshahi heard both the parties and allowed the appeal by the judgment and order dated 14.02.2008 reversing the order dated 2.11.2006 in Miscellaneous Case No. 48 of 2006 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bagha, Rajshahi. 

 8. The petitioner thereafter preferred Civil Revision No. 1879 of 2008 before the High Court Division against the judgment and order dated 14.02.2008 passed by the learned Appellate Court in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2007 and after hearing the High Court Division was pleased to dis-charge the Rule and vacate the order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule. 

 11. It appears that considering the facts and circumstances of the case the High Court Division rightly held that the order of injunction shield remain in force till disposal of the suit but this order shall have no bearing in deciding the title and possession of the parties in the land and house.
